preconditions: Use the committed test deck fixture.
steps: Wait for the deterministic parser result.
scenarios.oracle: The resolved card set and parser diagnostics match the fixture snapshot.

preconditions: A fixed deck and deterministic seed are loaded.
scenarios.oracle: The opening transaction and mulligan choice preserve the documented card counts and one-transaction undo boundary.

preconditions: The game is at a legal phase boundary with no unresolved stack item.
steps: Advance phases through the existing turn path.
Observe untap, draw, counters, and mana-pool boundaries.
scenarios.oracle: No acceptance pass/fail is claimed until CONFLICT-TURN-DRAW-001 receives an explicit ruling; preserve the existing turn path as evidence only.

preconditions: A card or linked object has a deterministic zone-change path.
steps: Inspect the resulting object identity and event record.
scenarios.oracle: Zone ownership, object identity, and last-known-information records obey the engine contract.

preconditions: A legal stack object is available.
steps: Advance priority and resolve or keep it guided.
scenarios.oracle: The shared stack preserves order, priority boundaries, and deterministic resolution output.

preconditions: A fixed mana pool and cost are supplied.
steps: Apply the transaction or receive its deterministic warning.
scenarios.oracle: Payment is deterministic, atomic, and leaves no partial state on failure.

preconditions: A fixed cost can be paid by a colored source and a five-color source.
steps: Plan payment with all sources untapped.
scenarios.oracle: The deterministic plan preserves the flexible source when a stricter source is sufficient.

preconditions: A required color is available only from a flexible source.
steps: Apply the selected source and cost.
scenarios.oracle: The flexible source supplies the required color and the payment completes without surplus taps.

preconditions: A cost can be paid by ordinary sources or a source with an explicit drawback.
steps: Inspect the chosen source set and warning boundary.
scenarios.oracle: Ordinary sources are preferred; a drawback source is selected only when it is necessary for a complete plan.

preconditions: A source produces a fixed multi-mana output.
steps: Inspect the generated mana bundle and payment.
scenarios.oracle: The exact mana bundle is generated once and the command does not over-tap.

preconditions: A fixed-cost mana ability needs a payment source before the spell payment.
scenarios.oracle: The activation and spell payment share one atomic transaction and one undo boundary.

preconditions: A sacrifice-based mana ability is necessary for a complete payment.
scenarios.oracle: The sacrifice choice follows the existing guided boundary and does not choose a commander while an ordinary source is sufficient.

preconditions: English Oracle text is pinned in a local fixture.
steps: Inspect the command plan and unsupported boundary.
scenarios.oracle: Only a replay-proven command plan is automatic; unsupported choices remain guided or manual.

preconditions: A committed command transaction exists.
steps: Redo it and compare the full snapshot.
scenarios.oracle: Undo and redo restore the exact prior and subsequent snapshots.

preconditions: A network-enabled verification lane is explicitly selected.
steps: Compare the response with the online contract.
scenarios.oracle: The live response is recorded only in the online lane and is not required by ordinary acceptance.

preconditions: Use one stable browser session and the fixed fixture route.
scenarios.oracle: The current interaction surface remains legible and usable at all three contract viewports with no console errors.

preconditions: An AV change is in scope and the browser audio policy permits playback.
steps: Check timing, audibility, reduced-motion behavior, and comfort.
scenarios.oracle: Human comfort and audibility are recorded only when AV behavior is changed; semantic event boundaries remain deterministic.

preconditions: A pinned CR clause and executable replay are available.
steps: Compare the final GameState and event stream.
scenarios.oracle: The final state and event sequence match the golden fixture; a partial effect is not reported as automatic.

preconditions: manual move
scenarios.oracle: geometry invents no meaning

preconditions: state disagrees with table
scenarios.oracle: human Correction wins

preconditions: bounded capability
scenarios.oracle: automation observable and correctable

preconditions: opening complete
scenarios.oracle: solo first and turn-zero manual opportunity

preconditions: phase boundaries
scenarios.oracle: stop behavior differs, authority does not

preconditions: progress pending
scenarios.oracle: HOLD identity-bound; ownership retained

preconditions: two commits
scenarios.oracle: one committed unit per Undo

preconditions: owner plus participant
scenarios.oracle: removal explicit; objects isolated, not Exile

preconditions: A bounded automation capability has produced state that the table explicitly corrects.
steps: Allow the same automation source to evaluate again without a new human action that reverses the correction.
scenarios.oracle: The later automation evaluation does not silently overwrite the human-confirmed Correction; any conflicting reapplication requires a new explicit attributable operation rather than implicit reassertion.

preconditions: Interaction context A is pending and a non-current player has requested HOLD for A.
steps: End or replace interaction context A before approval.
Attempt to approve or apply the old HOLD request.
scenarios.oracle: The HOLD request bound to A is stale and cannot rebind to B or grant foreground authority in B.

preconditions: Another player requests HOLD while the current operator owns progression.
steps: Submit HOLD request but do not approve it.
Inspect foreground operator, turn ownership, parent Resolution ownership and permitted progression controls.
scenarios.oracle: A request alone transfers no authority: the current operator retains foreground/progression authority and all parent ownership until explicit approval.

preconditions: During one Manual Resolution, operation A and operation B were committed separately before 処理完了, then 処理完了 closed the lifecycle.
steps: Invoke Undo again if a farther rewind is desired.
scenarios.oracle: One Undo reverts exactly one supported committed unit and does not collapse all pre-処理完了 operations into a mega-undo; farther rewind requires another invocation.

preconditions: A Ready Trigger is remembered while no canonical unresolved work otherwise forbids progression.
steps: Leave the Trigger remembered and visible.
Attempt an otherwise legal ordinary progression action in Normal interaction.
scenarios.oracle: Trigger Memory remains an ambient obligation and does not by itself become a global progress gate or steal foreground authority; only independently canonical unresolved work may block progression.
